subject: Human Body
title: Muscular Dystrophy
description: A micro-lesson that makes Muscular Dystrophy usable.

hook.text: Muscular dystrophy destroys muscle tissue over time. It's genetic and currently has no cure.

buildup.text: The most common form, Duchenne, affects boys. A faulty gene can't produce dystrophin, a vital structural protein.

discovery.text: Without dystrophin, muscle fibers tear during normal use and get replaced by fat and scar tissue.

twist.text: Symptoms appear by age 5. Most boys need a wheelchair by 12. The disease progresses relentlessly.

climax.text: Gene therapy trials aim to deliver working dystrophin genes. Early results give cautious hope.

punchline.text: One missing protein. One devastating disease. One race for a cure.

quiz.question: What causes Duchenne muscular dystrophy?
options: A virus that attacks muscle tissue
A genetic inability to produce dystrophin
